variants.name: functools.cached_property descriptor
variants.implementation_notes: Python's stdlib ships the value holder: functools.cached_property runs the getter on first attribute lookup and stores the result in the instance __dict__ under the same name, so later reads never call it again; since Python 3.12 the decorator no longer locks, and the docs record that two threads can therefore run the getter on first access. The hand-written equivalent is a @property plus a sentinel, which stays necessary when the attribute must be read-only, the class defines __slots__, or the loaded value needs explicit invalidation (del obj.attr).
pitfalls: cached_property needs a mutable instance __dict__: it fails on classes with __slots__ (without __dict__) and on metaclasses, and it caches nothing when the getter raises - the next access retries the query, the opposite of Go's OnceValues or .NET's Lazy<T>.
Since 3.12 there is no lock, so concurrent first access can run the loader twice (the getter must tolerate that); the cache also never expires - delete the attribute to invalidate it.
Detached ORM instances raise on first access (SQLAlchemy DetachedInstanceError): the session is part of the deferral contract, and serializing an ORM object can trigger the load unexpectedly.

variants.name: ORM-managed lazy relationship
variants.implementation_notes: The framework owns the marker: declare the association once ('author = models.ForeignKey(Author, on_delete=PROTECT)' in Django, 'author = relationship(Author, lazy="select")' in SQLAlchemy) and the mapper loads the related row through the session on first attribute access, caching it on the instance. Django collects rows for the needed associations with select_related/prefetch_related and SQLAlchemy with joinedload/selectinload - or forbids accidental loads with lazy='raise'. Choose it over a hand-rolled cached_property whenever the value is a mapped association, because identity, session and transaction semantics come for free.
variants.code_sketch:
class Book(Base):
    __tablename__ = "book"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    author_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("author.id"))
    author: Mapped["Author"] = relationship(lazy="select")   # on access
pitfalls: The load needs a live session: once it closes, the attribute raises (DetachedInstanceError) and cannot be loaded without re-attaching the instance.
Accessing the association inside a loop re-queries per instance; prefetch with selectinload/prefetch_related or forbid surprises with lazy='raise'.
Django and SQLAlchemy differ in naming and defaults (related managers versus relationship()): the policy lives in the mapping, so reviewing the mapping is what prevents N+1.
